terms.gloss: a vice, a fault, a failing
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.247: lēgibus et praemia prōposita sunt virtūtibus et supplicia vitiīs (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 1.1.41: virtūs est vitium fugere
terms.comment: Any fault or defect, of a body, a building, a speech, and above all of character, the opposite of virtūs. For a slip in writing see mistake; vitiō vertere is to count something as a fault in someone (Cic. Fam. 7.6.1).

evidence: Ter. Heaut. 5.2.20: quae ista est prāvitās? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally crookedness, deformity (Cic. Tusc. 4.29); of character, wrongheadedness rather than a particular vice.

phrases.english: they held that greed contained every vice

phrases.latin: ipsam verēcundiam, vitium quidem, sed amābile
phrases.english: shyness itself, a fault indeed, but a lovable one

phrases.latin: Quod aetās vitium posuit, aetās auferet.
phrases.english: what age has put there, age will take away
